title: Reranker Prefers the Glossary Over the Security Standard
summary: Dense retrieval finds the right standard, but the cross-encoder loves an exact-phrase glossary entry and pushes the alias-heavy gold chunk below the packing cutoff.
query: What security control does North Harbor use for break-glass access?

dataset.name: North Harbor security packet
dataset.notes: Synthetic enterprise-security corpus with a standard, FAQ, audit note, architecture brief, and incident retro.

debugChecklist: Compare retrieval order before and after reranking to see whether the gold chunk is being demoted.
Watch for alias-heavy documents whose wording is semantically right but lacks the exact surface form from the query.
If reranking hurts recall, test a no-rerank counterfactual before touching chunking or synthesis.

chunks.label: Standard chunk 1
chunks.text: Emergency elevation requests route through NH Vault, North Harbor's break-glass service, instead of going directly to an administrator.

chunks.label: Standard chunk 2
chunks.text: NH Vault uses dual-approval escrow: one human approver and one hardware-key release must both sign before privileged access is granted.

chunks.label: FAQ chunk 1
chunks.text: Break-glass access is the emergency path used when normal privilege workflows are unavailable during an incident.

chunks.label: Audit chunk 1
chunks.text: Auditors verified that emergency elevation always leaves an escrow record and requires two approvals before secrets are released.

chunks.label: Architecture chunk 1
chunks.text: North Harbor aliases its emergency broker as NH Vault in system diagrams, while internal tickets often call it the break-glass service.

chunks.label: Retro chunk 1
chunks.text: The on-call team recovered quickly because NH Vault released emergency credentials only after both approvers completed the escrow workflow.

runs.label: Baseline · reranker on

verdict.headline: The reranker boosted the glossary entry and demoted the standard that actually names the control.
verdict.detail: Retrieval already found the right standard, but reranking liked the surface phrase 'break-glass access' in the FAQ and pushed the gold control below the packed cutoff.

runs.story: This is a classic recall regression: reranking improves phrasing match but loses the substantive answer.
runs.outcome: The answer says break-glass is an emergency path, but never names the dual-approval escrow control.

runs.label: Fix · disable reranker

verdict.headline: Without the reranker, dense retrieval keeps the standard and audit note above the glossary.
verdict.detail: The candidate set already contained the right answer. Removing the reranker is enough to recover recall and ground the answer in the security standard.

runs.story: The simplest fix is to trust the retriever's semantic ranking instead of the phrase-heavy reranker.
runs.outcome: The answer now names dual-approval escrow as the controlling mechanism behind break-glass access.
